conventions.convention: For an epsilon-NFA, the input alphabet is Sigma; epsilon is transition notation for a move that consumes no input.
PDA stacks are words with the leftmost symbol at the top, and a move replaces that top symbol while leaving the suffix unchanged.
DPDAs recognize unmarked languages by accepting the marked inputs w dashv; the endmarker is not in the language alphabet.
One-tape tapes are right-infinite finite-support functions on natural-number cells, and a left move from cell 0 remains at cell 0.
A nondeterministic Turing machine accepts exactly when at least one finite accepting computation exists; other branches may diverge.
The configuration graph contains all configurations reachable by finitely many legal steps and may be infinite or cyclic.

load_bearing.statement: ECl(S) is defined through finite epsilon-transition chains starting at a state s in S, with the displayed chain written s=q_0,q_1,...,q_n=q.
The subset-construction DFA has state set P(Q), start state ECl(q_0), transition mu(S,a)=ECl(union_{q in S} delta(q,a)), and accepting subsets meeting F.
For every epsilon-NFA N, its subset-construction DFA D_N satisfies L(D_N)=L(N).
A PDA configuration is (q,w,alpha), with unread input w and leftmost stack top; the one-step relation pops the top symbol and replaces it by a stack word.
For every PDA, its final-state language is accepted by some empty-stack PDA and its empty-stack language by some final-state PDA.
For every CFG G, there exists a PDA M_G with N(M_G)=L(G).
For every PDA M, there is a fragment-variable CFG G_M with L(G_M)=N(M')=T(M), where M' is the converted empty-stack PDA.
A DPDA is specified with an endmarker and the stated restrictions on input-reading and epsilon moves; deterministic context-free languages are those it recognizes.
A deterministic one-tape TM has a total transition function on nonhalting state-symbol pairs and distinct accept and reject states.
A computation history starts at the initial configuration and follows one-step moves; divergence means that no halting computation history exists.
An NTM accepts w when a finite legal computation from its initial configuration ends in an accepting configuration.
G_N(w) has every finitely reachable configuration as a vertex and every legal one-step move as an arc.

concerns.concern: The displayed chain begins "s=q_0", but q_0 already denotes N's fixed start state. Read literally, the definition only permits epsilon-chains beginning at that start state and so does not define the epsilon-closure of an arbitrary S.

Its concluding characterization says epsilon moves may occur "before and between letter moves", but the recursion applies ECl after every letter; epsilon moves after the final letter must also be allowed.

The concatenation construction says to keep the accepting states of both copied machines while adding epsilon moves from accepting states of N_L to N_K. Then a word in L can still accept by stopping in an old accepting state of N_L, so the described machine recognizes at least L union LK rather than necessarily LK.
The two move clauses use a,w,Z,gamma,p,beta without explicitly quantifying them or stating their types. The intended domains are readily inferable, but the stated relation is not fully formal.

The final-state-to-empty-stack construction says to adjoin a fresh bottom marker B below the original stack but does not give an initial state and epsilon transition that install Z_0 above B; a PDA begins with only its designated initial stack symbol.

The forward inclusion is proved from a leftmost derivation, whereas L(G) was defined using arbitrary derivations. The needed standard conversion of a terminal derivation to a leftmost derivation is neither cited nor supplied.

In step 3.2, after splitting the remaining input into u and v, the first fragment is written (r,u,YWalpha) to (s,v,Walpha). With unread-input configurations, it should start with uv; as written the input accounting is inconsistent.

The definition limits delta(q,a,Z) to at most one pair only for a in Sigma union {dashv}; it places no at-most-one condition on delta(q,epsilon,Z). It therefore permits multiple enabled epsilon moves, contrary to the claimed determinism and the later unique-computation lemma.
The configuration-word definition uses r=max({h} union supp(t)) but its local dependencies establish finite support without stating the finite-nonempty-subset maximum fact needed for that expression.
The head-update cases use h+1, h-1, and h>0 although the local cited configuration convention only establishes h in N; the arithmetic and predecessor convention are left unstated.
